clue.text: Woman writer in club

parts.note: at means in, as in at home
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A female author is spotted at a club or society.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Atwood is the Canadian novelist behind The Handmaid's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Atwood is a celebrated Canadian novelist, so she is a female author.

clue.text: Sign Heartbeat singer

indicators.note: beat as in battered or knocked about tells us to mix up the word heart

parts.note: Cher is the famous American pop singer

explanation.surface: A pop star signs up to sing on the TV drama Heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'Heart beat' together as 'Heartbeat', the British TV police drama, which hides that 'beat' is the anagram signal. Cher is the American pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius, a sign of the zodiac, is represented by a bowman.

clue.text: Wanting Blades to beat Owls, reason won out

indicators.note: to beat means to batter about, so the letters of owls and reason are mixed, with won removed as the clue's out says

explanation.surface: A Sheffield derby: the Blades want to beat the Owls, and reason lost out.
explanation.walkthrough: Blades (Sheffield United) and Owls (Sheffield Wednesday) are rival English football clubs. Mix OWLS and REASON, then take out the letters of WON ('won out').
explanation.definitionFit: Blades are the flat ends of oars, so a boat lacking them is without oars.

clue.text: Pulls turf up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sward is grassy turf

explanation.surface: Someone tears up the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to pull or drag something along.

clue.text: They don't appreciate 'smart 'is irritating

parts.note: in means fashionable, smart
a dropped-aitch 'his', read as is, irritating: grates means is irritating

explanation.surface: A cockney complains that a smart-alec's manner is getting on his nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes paint a dropped-aitch accent; they do not change the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungrateful people fail to show thanks, so they fail to appreciate what they are given.

clue.text: Fancy Tories! True embarrassingly but that's not illegal

indicators.note: embarrassingly suggests the three words are thrown into disarray and rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on how awkwardly the Tories are being fancied, said to be perfectly lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb or exclamation, but it is part of the fodder with TORIES and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a retort meaning nobody can stop you, since the action is permitted by law.

clue.text: Gets to do a play which isn't vulgar

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are moved around freely

explanation.surface: Someone gets to stage a refined, tasteful production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun after 'a', but it signals the rearrangement of GETS TO DO A.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement in style is the quality that avoids anything coarse or crude.

clue.text: Gives evidence for state about street uprising

indicators.note: an uprising is a revolt or riot, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A witness testifies about a revolt in the streets of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' mixes STATE and ST into the answer; 'about' is a link meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch for something is to give testimony that confirms it.

clue.text: Scriptures are uplifting-an inspiration

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the run of letters is read upwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a body of scripture

explanation.surface: Holy writ is described as uplifting and inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry; the Muses are proverbial sources of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, the goddesses who inspire artists.

clue.text: Long shots? Um… one's come in — the drinks are on us

indicators.note: come in tells us the hesitation and the a are placed inside the wagers

parts.note: long shots are wagers, bets at long odds
erm is a hesitant 'um'
a means one

explanation.surface: A punter hesitates as an outsider wins and offers to buy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic reading: drinks stand on these mats in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard coasters in a pub are what glasses rest upon.

clue.text: Expenditure dismissed by woman spending five hundred

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

indicators.note: spending means giving away, so the letter is lost from the word

parts.note: a lady is a woman
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A woman spending five hundred pounds is turned out for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent, a cost or expense.

clue.text: Amateur taking part over? Right

indicators.note: over means the selected letters are turned back to front
part means only a portion of the words amateur taking is used

explanation.surface: An amateur asks whether the game is over and is told he is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EURT straddles 'Amateur taking'; 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and accurate are both senses shared with this word.

clue.text: Like taking ecstasy (wrapped in paper) and crack -it's for when pot's not available

definitions.text: it's for when pot's not available

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside, so the paper and drug go within

parts.note: say means for example, like

indicators.note: the drug letter is enclosed by the newspaper abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
E is the drug ecstasy
a crack is an attempt, a shot

explanation.surface: Drug-taking advice: roll some ecstasy in paper, or crack, when there's no cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is a snooker pot, not cannabis: a snooker player who cannot pot a ball plays defensively.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, a defensive stroke is played when no ball can be sunk.

clue.text: See 26
Borrow book by top golfer saving a lot of energy

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe inside

parts.note: Rory McIlroy is a leading golfer
many means a lot
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone borrows a book written by a leading golfer about saving energy.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow wrote the 1857 novel The Romany Rye; 'Borrow' looks like a verb but is the author.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany Rye is a novel by the Victorian writer George Borrow.

clue.text: Extremely tense leaving dangerous area of London

parts.note: so means extremely, as in so good

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter goes out

parts.note: hot can mean dangerous, as in too hot to handle
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: Feeling very tense, someone gets out of a risky part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district in central London known for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of the West End in the British capital.

clue.text: She's working in theatre

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: An actress is employed on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Famous horse not about to get beat

indicators.note: not means the letters are left out

parts.note: Red Rum won the Grand National three times
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A famous racehorse is not about to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the British racehorse that won the Grand National steeplechase three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to strike rhythmically, to beat.

clue.text: Parent power, some say, polarising response

indicators.note: some say means the words are spoken and heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: ma is a parent and might means power

explanation.surface: Parent power is said by some to provoke divided opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: MA MIGHT spoken in a non-rhotic British accent matches the yeast spread; Marmite advertised itself as 'love it or hate it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British yeast spread is famous for being loved or loathed, the archetype of divisive taste.

clue.text: Modern prophet in fancy hotel with female — a knockout

indicators.note: in here says the prophet's surname sits within the exclamation, enclosed by its two letters

parts.note: My! and Fancy! are both exclamations of surprise
David Icke is a conspiracy theorist who once proclaimed himself a son of God
an inn is a hotel

explanation.surface: A modern seer in a smart hotel with a woman ends up knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the hotel, but it is the exclamation 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drugged drink is something that knocks the drinker unconscious.

clue.text: Fleet clear rock

parts.note: fleet means fast, swift
net means clear, as in net profit

explanation.surface: A navy fleet clears a dangerous rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fastnet is a rock off southern Ireland, famous for its yacht race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fastnet is an islet off the Irish coast with a lighthouse.

clue.text: Sick of hearing about United, OK?

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece
sick means unwell or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: U is short for United in football club names

explanation.surface: A fan is fed up with hearing about Manchester United, all right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick of' looks like a phrase, but 'Sick' is the anagram signal and 'of' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions signal acceptance or agreement, like saying all right.

clue.text: Author Henry in religious sect

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis are English authors
H is the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A writer called Henry belongs to a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The henry (H) is the SI unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Christian group in North America.

clue.text: Clear howler for middle name of popular President -Walker!

indicators.note: for middle means the central letters of howler are cleared out and swapped for the new piece

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, famous from the slogan I like Ike

explanation.surface: A gaffe about a President's middle name involving the word Walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' asks you to empty the middle of HOWLER, leaving H...R, and put IKE in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler on foot is a walker.

clue.text: Hide from unlimited questioning

indicators.note: unlimited means losing the bounding letters at each end

parts.note: asking means questioning

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from endless interrogation.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its pelt.

clue.text: 'Hairier bum!' I cried

indicators.note: bum means bad or faulty, so the letters are arranged wrongly

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in shock at a hairy backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the backside but is slang for poor quality, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy means risky in slang, so its comparative means more risky.

clue.text: Riot tanks -these get deployed with proletariat finally -------

definitions.text: Riot tanks -these get deployed with proletariat finally

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of proletariat is taken
deployed means sent out and arranged, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolution: workers face the riot tanks sent out against them.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dashes stand for the answer completing the sentence. RIOT TANKS THESE GET plus the T from 'proletariat finally' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters marching in public are what tanks are sent against in a revolt.

clue.text: Knocking off time — hurry greatly

parts.note: hie is an old word for hurry
very means greatly

explanation.surface: At knocking-off time, everyone hurries home quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking off' looks like finishing work but is British slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock off is slang for to steal, and stealing is theft.

clue.text: He's horrible to crew members backing force

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the sailors are read in reverse

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a tar is a sailor
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: A nasty man forces crew members into retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratbag is a nasty, despicable person.
